# Route Handlers Registry

> **Registry commands in this guide** run in the NextSpark monorepo, from the repository root. In a generated project, `nextspark prepare` generates the registries together with `src/app`, and `nextspark dev` regenerates them as sources change.

**Auto-generated by `nextspark prepare` • API route metadata only • No handler is imported or executed**

---

## Overview

The Route Handlers Registry (`.nextspark/registries/route-handlers.ts`) lists the API routes of a project as **documentation metadata**: the API Explorer and the devtools read it through `ApiRoutesService` (see [Usage](./07-route-handlers-usage.md)).

It holds no handler. There is no runtime dispatcher (`/api/v1/theme/**` and `/api/v1/plugin/**` were removed in `0.1.0-beta.192`): the generated host writes every project route (`api/**/route.ts`) and every plugin route (`plugins/<name>/api/**/route.ts`) as a route file of its own in `src/app`, and Next.js serves it directly.

| Route source | File in the project | Served at |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Project | `api/<path>/route.ts` | `/api/<path>` |
| Plugin | `plugins/<name>/api/<path>/route.ts` | `/api/plugins/<name>/<path>` |
| Core | shipped by `@nextsparkjs/core` | `/api/v1/**` |
| Entity | generated from the entity config | `/api/v1/<entity>` and `/api/v1/<entity>/[id]` |

`/api/v1/**` belongs to core: a project route there stops generation, and replacing a core route on purpose goes through `templates/api/v1/...`. A project can also replace the generic handler of one of its own entities with `templates/api/v1/<entity>/[id]/route.ts` (or `route.ts`, `[id]/child/[childType]/route.ts`, `[id]/child/[childType]/[childId]/route.ts`); see [Overriding an entity's API](../05-api/04-custom-endpoints.md#overriding-an-entitys-api).

---

## Registry structure

```typescript
// .nextspark/registries/route-handlers.ts (generated, do not edit)

export interface ApiRouteEntry {
  path: string
  methods: string[]
  category: 'core' | 'entity' | 'theme' | 'plugin'
  source?: string
  subcategory?: string
}

export const API_ROUTES_METADATA: {
  core: ApiRouteEntry[]
  entities: ApiRouteEntry[]
  theme: ApiRouteEntry[]   // the project's own api/ routes
  plugins: ApiRouteEntry[]
}

export const API_ROUTES_SUMMARY: {
  totalRoutes: number
  byCategory: { core: number; entities: number; theme: number; plugins: number }
  generatedAt: string
}
```

The `theme` category holds the routes of the project's `api/` folder (the name is kept for compatibility with the devtools). The generator reads each `route.ts` and records the HTTP methods it exports (`GET`, `POST`, `PUT`, `PATCH`, `DELETE`).

---

## Dynamic segments

A route folder named `[id]` or `[...path]` is a normal Next.js dynamic segment: `api/orders/[id]/route.ts` is served at `/api/orders/<id>`, and the registry lists it as `/api/orders/[id]`. Core's own dynamic routes (`api/v1/[entity]/**`) are listed as the per-entity routes they serve.
